html:
The Mongol state in Iran and Iraq, founded by Hulegu, a grandson of Genghis Khan, and ruled by his descendants from 1256 to 1335. Its rulers called their realm Iran.

Hulegu was sent west by his brother, the Great Khan Mongke. He destroyed the castles of the Nizari Ismailis, the so-called Assassins, in 1256 and sacked Baghdad in 1258. When Mongke died in 1259 the Mongol Empire split, and Hulegu kept the southwest as his own. His advance into Syria was stopped by the Mamluks at Ain Jalut in 1260.

The Ilkhans were hemmed in by enemies: the Mamluks to the west and their own cousins of the Golden Horde to the north. Their friends were in the east, in Yuan China, ruled by Hulegu's brother Kublai. That link carried Chinese painting, medicine and paper money ideas into Iran, and Persian astronomy east. Hulegu funded the Maragheh observatory under the scholar Nasir al-Din al-Tusi.

In 1295 Ghazan Khan became a Muslim, and Islam became the state faith. His vizier Rashid al-Din wrote the Compendium of Chronicles, an early attempt at a history of the whole known world.

When Abu Said died in 1335 without an heir, the state broke into local dynasties. Timur later conquered most of its lands.
sum: The Mongol state in Iran and Iraq, founded by Hulegu, a grandson of Genghis Khan, and ruled by his descendants from 1256 to 1335. Its rulers called their realm Iran.
